# Tapanīya Sutta (Iti 30 (It 2.3 PTS It 24))

**ID:** Iti 30 (It 2.3 PTS It 24)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Tapanīya Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Mortifying
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti30
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tapanīya Sutta* ("Mortifying", Iti 30) is the third discourse in the second chapter (Dukanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The discourse addresses two states that cause remorse and torment (*dhammā tapanīyā*), arising from the realization of having engaged in misconduct (bodily, verbal, and mental) while failing to cultivate wholesome conduct [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2012]. Mrs. Rhys Davids notes that *tapanīya* denotes "burning" states of conscience experienced when reflecting on having done what ought not to have been done and having neglected what ought to have been done [Mrs. Rhys Davids, Buddhism]. The ethical category of *tapanīyā dhammā* versus *atapanīyā dhammā* also constitutes an established dyad in the Abhidhamma *mātika* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, where *tapanīya* states are formally defined as bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct that burn or torment the mind with remorse [Rhys Davids 1900; Müller 1885; Tan 2015].

According to SuttaCentral, the discourse has a full parallel in Chinese translation (T 765.65) and an internal passage-level parallel in the *Duccarita Sutta* (Iti 64) [SuttaCentral]. Resembling parallels are found in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 140), *Gāndhārī Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 201–223), *Udānavarga* (UV 28), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5.174, AN 6.45) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus indicates substantial Pali-internal text reuse with the *Dukanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 2; 53 matches, particularly §2.1–2.3 aligning with §3.1.1–3.1.3), along with near-verbatim alignment across §0.1–5.1 with the paired *Atapanīya Sutta* (Iti 31) [DharmaNexus]. Additional text reuse is recorded with the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37), the *Sucarita Sutta* (Iti 65), and the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), alongside cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (增壹阿含經, T 125, fascicle 12) [DharmaNexus].
